episodes.name: 1973-74 oil shock and stagflation
episodes.broke: OPEC embargo quadrupled oil; inflation above 10 %; the Nifty Fifty de-rated; S&P 500 -48 %.
episodes.policy: Price controls (failed), then the Fed tightened into the downturn.
episodes.gap: Inflation expectations were not anchored - policy credibility, not a rule, was missing.
episodes.lesson: Valuation on 'can't-miss' growth stocks does not survive an inflation and rate shock.

episodes.name: 1980-82 Volcker tightening
episodes.broke: Fed funds near 20 %; double-dip recession; LDC (Latin-American) debt crisis followed in 1982.
warnings: bank lending to developing countries (petrodollar recycling)
episodes.policy: Volcker held rates high; banks' LDC losses were forborne for years (regulatory forbearance).
episodes.gap: Bank capital on sovereign loans - Basel I came in 1988.
episodes.lesson: Disinflation by recession; forbearance hid bank losses for a decade.

episodes.name: 1987 crash
episodes.broke: The Dow fell 22.6 % on 10-19-87; portfolio insurance sold into a falling market.
episodes.policy: Fed liquidity statement on 10-20; no firm bail-outs.
episodes.gap: Market structure (portfolio insurance, no circuit breakers) - circuit breakers came in 1988.
episodes.lesson: A rate shock into stretched prices can crash a market without a recession.

episodes.name: 1990-91 recession: S&L, real estate, oil
episodes.broke: Savings & loans failed on bad real-estate loans; oil doubled after Iraq invaded Kuwait; bank credit crunch.
episodes.policy: FIRREA / Resolution Trust Corp (1989): ~$124 bn of taxpayer losses - the S&L bail-out.
episodes.gap: Deposit insurance without risk-based premiums or capital - moral hazard.
episodes.lesson: Insured deposits funding real-estate speculation: the taxpayer was the backstop.

episodes.name: 1994 bond massacre
episodes.broke: The Fed doubled rates (3 % -> 6 %) in a year; bond losses; Orange County bankrupt; Mexico's peso crisis.
warnings: first hike after a long hold
episodes.policy: US Exchange Stabilization Fund loans to Mexico (~$20 bn) - a sovereign bail-out.
episodes.gap: Leverage in derivatives (inverse floaters) outside bank capital rules.
episodes.lesson: A rate shock finds the leverage that assumed rates would stay low.

episodes.name: 1998 Russia / LTCM
episodes.broke: Russia defaulted; LTCM's ~25x leveraged convergence trades blew up; credit and liquidity froze.
episodes.policy: The Fed organised a private $3.6 bn recapitalisation of LTCM and cut rates three times - the 'Greenspan put'.
episodes.gap: Hedge-fund leverage and OTC derivatives were unregulated.
episodes.lesson: Rescuing leverage teaches leverage; the 1999 mania followed the 1998 rescue.

episodes.name: 2000-02 dot-com bubble
episodes.broke: Nasdaq -78 %; telecom over-build and vendor financing (Lucent, Nortel lent to customers to buy their gear) failed; accounting frauds (Enron 2001, WorldCom 2002).
warnings: stock market value / GDP at a record (~180 %)
IPO frenzy - hundreds of unprofitable IPOs a year, first-day pops ~70 % in 1999
Fed +1.75 pts (June 1999 - May 2000) into the mania
credit spreads and high-yield defaults rising from 1998
telecom capex and debt; vendor financing
narrowing breadth - most stocks fell in 1999 while the index rose
episodes.policy: Fed cut 6.5 % -> 1.75 %; no bail-out of dot-coms; Sarbanes-Oxley (2002) and the Global Research Settlement (2003) on conflicted analysts.
episodes.gap: Underwriter-analyst conflicts (buy ratings on banking clients), off-balance-sheet vehicles (Enron SPEs), IPO laddering / spinning.
episodes.lesson: Price far ahead of profits, funded by the sellers themselves (vendor financing) and cheered by conflicted research - rhymes with any circular build-out.

episodes.name: 2007-09 financial crisis
episodes.broke: Subprime mortgages defaulted; AAA tranches failed; asset-backed commercial paper froze (Aug 2007); Lehman failed; S&P -57 %.
warnings: ABCP and interbank funding seized Aug 2007
marginal buyers (German regional banks) stopped buying CDOs in summer 2007
episodes.policy: TARP ($700 bn), Fed emergency facilities, Fannie / Freddie conservatorship, AIG rescue - bail-outs of the system.
episodes.gap: Shadow banking (SIVs, ABCP, repo), ratings models assuming 7-10 % losses, CDS without capital (AIG).
episodes.lesson: The loss data led by a year; the funding markets were the trigger; bail-outs socialised the losses.

episodes.name: 2010 euro sovereign scare / flash crash
episodes.broke: Greece lost market access; bank funding in euros stressed; the 5-6-2010 flash crash.
episodes.policy: EU / IMF bail-out of Greece (€110 bn).
episodes.gap: No euro-area fiscal backstop; the sovereign-bank doom loop.
episodes.lesson: Sovereigns can be the marginal borrower that fails.

episodes.name: 2011 euro crisis / US downgrade
episodes.broke: Italy / Spain spreads blew out; S&P downgraded the US (8-5-2011); S&P 500 -19 %.
episodes.gap: A central bank as the only buyer of last resort.
episodes.lesson: Funding stress spreads across borders through banks.

episodes.name: 2015-16 oil collapse / China / high-yield energy
episodes.broke: Oil -75 %; high-yield energy defaults; China's devaluation (Aug 2015); an industrial recession.
episodes.policy: Fed delayed hikes; China capital controls.
episodes.gap: Shale capex funded by high-yield debt at $100 oil.
episodes.lesson: Debt-funded capex on a commodity price fails when the price does.

episodes.name: 2018 Q4 tightening scare
episodes.broke: Fed hikes plus balance-sheet run-off; S&P 500 -20 %; credit spreads widened.
warnings: fed funds +1 pt and quantitative tightening
episodes.gap: Markets priced on a central bank 'put'.
episodes.lesson: Liquidity withdrawal hits the most expensive assets first.

episodes.name: 2020 COVID crash
episodes.broke: Pandemic shutdown; the dash for cash broke the Treasury market; S&P 500 -34 % in 23 sessions.
warnings: none in credit or loss data - an exogenous shock
episodes.policy: Fed bought corporate bonds and backstopped everything; CARES Act - the broadest bail-out on record.
episodes.gap: Open-end bond funds and Treasury market liquidity.
episodes.lesson: Not every crash is forecastable; leverage decides how bad it gets.

episodes.name: 2022 inflation and rate shock
episodes.broke: CPI 9 %; the Fed +4.25 pts in a year; Nasdaq -35 %, bonds -17 %; crypto and SPAC collapse.
warnings: SPAC and IPO frenzy in 2021 (a dot-com rhyme)
episodes.policy: No bail-outs; the Fed's fastest hiking cycle since 1981.
episodes.gap: Duration risk on bank balance sheets (held-to-maturity accounting) - it surfaced in 2023.
episodes.lesson: Money-printing and a speculative frenzy, then a rate shock - 2000's structure in a new costume.

episodes.name: 2023 regional bank run (SVB, Signature, First Republic)
episodes.broke: Unrealised losses on banks' bond portfolios plus concentrated uninsured deposits; a digital bank run.
episodes.policy: Systemic-risk exception (uninsured depositors made whole) and the Bank Term Funding Program - a depositor bail-out.
episodes.gap: Held-to-maturity accounting hid rate losses; 2018 rules eased oversight of mid-size banks.
episodes.lesson: The 2022 shock found the gap the 2010 rules left; the bail-out covered it again.

method: Each indicator is scored against its own history (expanding window, publication lags respected: no hindsight); pillars average their indicators, the gauges average their pillars; risk = the composite's percentile vs its own history. Bottom-up readings are scored against our daily history once 40 days exist (provisional anchors before).
caveats: Backtest uses today's revised data, not what was published at the time (revisions can be large around turns).
Publication lags are approximations per series.
Few recessions in the sample (1990, 2001, 2008, 2020): hit rates are indicative, not statistics.
The 2020 recession was an exogenous shock - no credit indicator could have led it.
A warning is a probability shift, not a timing call: 2006's data were early by a year.
